criteria.name: Reproduction steps present
criteria.autoCheck: Look for numbered list or 'Steps to Reproduce' / 'Repro' section

criteria.name: Expected vs actual behavior documented
criteria.autoCheck: Look for 'Expected' and 'Actual' sections or descriptions

criteria.name: Acceptance criteria can close in phase
criteria.autoCheck: For each AC, ask which workflow phase owns its completion condition: implementation (resolves while the issue is worked), review (resolves after in_review), or release (resolves during /prepare-release). At the moment /work reaches Step 5 and gh pmu validates the checkboxes, is the condition knowably true? If not the AC is out of phase. This is NOT the same question as ac-testable / success-measurable, which ask whether a condition is well-defined — 'once released and re-imported, the config is revisited' is perfectly measurable and simply is not measurable YET. Re-read .claude/metadata/ac-feasibility-prompts.json from disk and apply phaseFeasibility.actionIfOutOfPhase: work listed in ownedElsewhere (CHANGELOG, tagging, release publication) should be DROPPED, not annotated, because another command's checklist already discharges it; a genuinely load-bearing gate should be ANNOTATED per annotationFormat with a gatePhases token. Report ❌ for an out-of-phase AC carrying no annotation, ⚠️ for one whose annotation is present but questionable. Also check each existing annotation in BOTH directions: a `→ GATE:` token whose AC text names no event that resolves it is reported (the token is being used to mean 'I cannot tick this now' rather than as a phase claim), and so is one whose named condition no gate phase describes or which is in fact satisfiable during implementation. An annotation is a claim about phase, not a license to leave a box unchecked.

criteria.name: Environment info present
criteria.autoCheck: Look for 'Environment', browser, OS, version references

criteria.name: Severity proportionate to impact
criteria.autoCheck: Re-read .claude/metadata/bug-priority-rubric.json from disk. Match the bug's stated impact (Description, Actual Behavior, Scope, Deployment Impact) against each class's description and signals, apply the rubric's precedence (highest matching priority wins; no match → fallback), and compare the result to the issue's board priority. Evidence names the matched class id, the rubric priority and the current priority. Mismatch → ⚠️ naming the rubric priority, which /resolve-review proposes (#2992)

criteria.name: Test coverage proportionate (bug)
criteria.autoCheck: Regression-test AC required unless the issue states why one is not warranted (e.g. the defect is in prose or data with no executable path): the AC must reproduce the reported behavior, because existing tests did not catch the defect — which is why 'existing tests pass' alone does not suffice even for a single-path fix. Flag ⚠️ when neither a regression-test AC nor a stated reason is present (#2993). Multi-path refactor: ACs MUST require tests for new pattern (flag if only 'existing tests pass' for changes touching multiple functions/modules). Additionally report which test files the fix implicates, pairing inferred source paths against `.claude/skills/tdd-refactor-coverage-audit/resources/test-coverage-conventions.json` and naming each; where no pairing resolves, say that none could be resolved and why rather than reporting nothing. Advisory — blocks nothing.

criteria.name: Proposed fix described
criteria.autoCheck: Check for 'Proposed Fix', 'Root Cause Analysis', 'Fix Approach', or solution description section. Treat as missing if section body is under 20 characters or contains placeholder text ('To be documented', 'TBD', '...')

criteria.name: Files to modify declared at top level
criteria.autoCheck: Pipe the body to the helper — gh pmu view <N> --body-stdout | node .claude/scripts/shared/lib/declared-scope-check.js — never through a temp file, whose root write would void a concurrent Tier 3 review (#3351); report the status it returns with its evidence; do not re-parse the block here — the helper reuses scope-drift-check.js parseDeclaredScope. pass -> ✅ with the parsed paths as evidence. warn -> ⚠️ naming the problem the evidence states: a header not at top level (off its own line, or inside a list item such as a Steps to Reproduce step — #3239, which concurrency-plan then classified undeclared and sent to the sequential tail), parseDeclaredScope's warning (section found but no backticked paths parsed), or no top-level declaration at all. Step 2a-ii (b) writes the declaration after this evaluation: when it does, re-run the helper on the written body and report that result, naming the repair. Advisory — a warning, never ❌.

criteria.name: Root cause identified
criteria.autoCheck: Does the body state WHY the defect happens — the mechanism: the specific code path, condition or data that produces the wrong behavior — anywhere in Description, Actual Behavior or Proposed Fix? Distinct from proposed-fix-described, which asks WHAT the fix does. ✅ when the mechanism is stated. ✅ also when the body explicitly says the root cause is not yet known and names the investigation that will establish it — at filing time an honest 'unknown' is correct. ⚠️ when the body only restates the symptom. Advisory, never ❌: an unknown root cause must not block the review (#2993).

criteria.name: Deployment impact assessed
criteria.autoCheck: Check for a 'Deployment Impact' section (or 'Impact: dev-only' / 'Impact: deployed') in the body. Validate the classification against framework-manifest.json deploymentFiles - the authority the issue corpus actually reasons from - together with the Stage 1 / Stage 2 command pipeline and deploy-dist.yml. Values: 'dev-only' = touches nothing that reaches a user project (framework scripts, Proposal/, PRD/, Archive/, tests, CHANGELOG); 'deployed' = touches a path carried by deploymentFiles or emitted by Stage 2, so it reaches user projects on hub update - list the affected areas; 'unknown' = the classification could not be determined and needs a human decision before the issue is worked.

criteria.name: Prior art checked
criteria.autoCheck: Delegate to decideSweep in .claude/scripts/shared/lib/prior-art-marker.js and report the status it returns; do not re-derive the rule here. The marker itself is the literal '**Prior Art:**' heading defined by .claude/metadata/prior-art-sweep.json bodyFormat.heading; present and complete = pass. Issues created before the cutoff in that helper are not applicable rather than failing. Behavior past that depends on framework-config.json reviewSweep, a 4-mode setting since #2564 (absent = 'recommend'): under 'full' an absent or PARTIAL marker reports fail and runs the Step 2a-iv sweep; under 'recommend' it reports the advisory status 'recommend' and runs NO sweep — this must NOT be reported as fail, because --prior-art is opt-in and rarely passed, so most issues carry no marker and a fail would downgrade nearly every review; under 'flag-only' and 'off' report skip, not fail, which would downgrade every review in a project that opted out.

criteria.name: Scope supports incremental implementation
criteria.autoCheck: Check if ACs are small, independent, testable units (not monolithic)

criteria.name: Depends on line resolves
criteria.autoCheck: Read the `**Depends on:**` line (#3127) with `.claude/scripts/shared/lib/depends-on.js` `parseDependsOn(body, {self, members})`, where `members` is the parent epic's or branch tracker's sub-issue numbers (`gh pmu sub list <parent> --json`). Report ❌ for each entry the parser rejects: unresolvable (not a `#N` reference — `#abc`, `Story 1.1`, a bare number), non-member (a number outside the parent's sub-issue set), or self-referential (the issue's own number). A rejected entry yields no edge, and a dependency nobody can read is never treated as satisfied, so an unattended `--nonstop` or `--concurrent` run would order around it blind. A missing line is not a finding — it is every story authored before the line existed; `none` is an explicit empty list. A story with no parent cannot be checked for membership: say so rather than reporting ✅.

criteria.name: Test coverage proportionate (story)
criteria.autoCheck: Infer scope from ACs and description. If story adds or modifies code paths, ACs should include test requirements proportionate to scope. Additionally report which test files the story implicates, pairing inferred source paths against `.claude/skills/tdd-refactor-coverage-audit/resources/test-coverage-conventions.json` and naming each; where no pairing resolves, say that none could be resolved and why rather than reporting nothing. A story authored through /add-story should already carry candidate test paths in its `**Files to modify:**` section (#2727) — their absence is itself worth reporting. Advisory — blocks nothing.

criteria.name: Iterate and review each sub-issue
criteria.autoCheck: Expand the epic into the multi-issue set: read the children from `gh pmu sub list <epic> --json` and review each child as its own issue through Steps 1-3 — own preamble, own type criteria, Step 2a-ii proposed solution/fix auto-generate with per-sub-issue body updates, own finalize — so each child earns its own review comment, `**Reviews:** N` marker and label. The children are reviewed before the epic, so evaluate this criterion from their recorded outcomes: pass only when every child was reached, fail otherwise, and in both cases record the roster — each child reviewed with its verdict, each child not reached with the reason (the expansion cap resolveReviewExpansion returns — framework-config.json reviewExpansion.expansionCap, its default when absent — error, interrupted) — as this criterion's evidence in the epic's own review comment. Never expand a child that is itself an epic.
